title: Pendulum Motion (simple, and with a nail constraint)
theory: Tension does no work, so **energy conservation gives the speed at any height**; the **radial Newton equation gives the tension**. With a nail a distance $b$ below the pivot, the instant the string touches it the radius shrinks from $a$ to $a-b$ and the center jumps to the nail. The string stays taut only while $T \ge 0$: at angle $\theta$ from the *upward* vertical of the current center, $T = \frac{mv^2}{r} - mg\cos\theta$, so slack begins when $v^2 = gr\cos\theta$. Completing a full loop of radius $r$ requires $v_{top}^2 \ge gr$. (Plain small-angle pendulum: $T = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$ — mass- and amplitude-independent.)
framework: Energy → $v^2$ at the point of interest.

parts.title: Speed at B
parts.parameters:
- Given: ball $m$ on a string of length $a$ from pivot O; released from rest at A, level with O; a nail at C, a distance $b$ straight below O, with $a/2 < b < a$; B is the lowest point (depth $a$); D is the top of the small circle about C; gravity $g$; no air resistance.
- Find: speed and tension at B; tension at D; taut-string condition; slack speed for $b=a/2$.
- Diagram: big circle (radius $a$, center O) down to B; past B the string wraps the nail → small circle (radius $a-b$, center C); D sits $a-b$ above C, i.e. at depth $2b-a$ below O.
parts.conclusion: the nail is irrelevant until the string is vertical — energy only sees depth.

parts.title: Tension just before B
parts.parameters:
- Given: ball $m$ on a string of length $a$ from pivot O; released from rest at A, level with O; a nail at C, a distance $b$ straight below O, with $a/2 < b < a$; B is the lowest point (depth $a$); D is the top of the small circle about C; gravity $g$; no air resistance.
- Find: speed and tension at B; tension at D; taut-string condition; slack speed for $b=a/2$.
- Diagram: big circle (radius $a$, center O) down to B; past B the string wraps the nail → small circle (radius $a-b$, center C); D sits $a-b$ above C, i.e. at depth $2b-a$ below O.
parts.conclusion: the universal "released from the pivot's level" result: **T = 3mg at the bottom**. Memorize it.

parts.title: Tension at D (top of the small circle)
parts.parameters:
- Given: ball $m$ on a string of length $a$ from pivot O; released from rest at A, level with O; a nail at C, a distance $b$ straight below O, with $a/2 < b < a$; B is the lowest point (depth $a$); D is the top of the small circle about C; gravity $g$; no air resistance.
- Find: speed and tension at B; tension at D; taut-string condition; slack speed for $b=a/2$.
- Diagram: big circle (radius $a$, center O) down to B; past B the string wraps the nail → small circle (radius $a-b$, center C); D sits $a-b$ above C, i.e. at depth $2b-a$ below O.
parts.formulas: depth of D below O: $b - (a-b) = 2b-a$ ⇒ $v_D^2 = 2g(2b-a)$; top of circle: $T + mg = \frac{mv_D^2}{a-b}$.
parts.conclusion: with $a/2<b<a$ the denominator is positive, so the sign of $(5b-3a)$ decides everything — which is exactly part (4).

parts.title: Condition to reach D with the string taut
parts.parameters:
- Given: ball $m$ on a string of length $a$ from pivot O; released from rest at A, level with O; a nail at C, a distance $b$ straight below O, with $a/2 < b < a$; B is the lowest point (depth $a$); D is the top of the small circle about C; gravity $g$; no air resistance.
- Find: speed and tension at B; tension at D; taut-string condition; slack speed for $b=a/2$.
- Diagram: big circle (radius $a$, center O) down to B; past B the string wraps the nail → small circle (radius $a-b$, center C); D sits $a-b$ above C, i.e. at depth $2b-a$ below O.
parts.conclusion: equivalently $b > \frac{3}{5}a$. Same physics as the loop-the-loop criterion, dressed for the exam.

parts.title: Slack speed when b = a/2
parts.parameters:
- Given: ball $m$ on a string of length $a$ from pivot O; released from rest at A, level with O; a nail at C, a distance $b$ straight below O, with $a/2 < b < a$; B is the lowest point (depth $a$); D is the top of the small circle about C; gravity $g$; no air resistance.
- Find: speed and tension at B; tension at D; taut-string condition; slack speed for $b=a/2$.
- Diagram: big circle (radius $a$, center O) down to B; past B the string wraps the nail → small circle (radius $a-b$, center C); D sits $a-b$ above C, i.e. at depth $2b-a$ below O.
parts.formulas: radius $r = a/2$; at angle $\theta$ from C's upward vertical: energy $v^2 = 2g\left(b - r\cos\theta\right) = ga(1-\cos\theta)$; slack: $v^2 = gr\cos\theta = \frac{ga}{2}\cos\theta$.
parts.conclusion: two equations (energy, $T=0$) in two unknowns ($v$, $\theta$). $\cos\theta = 2/3 > 0$ means the string goes slack *above* C's horizontal — projectile motion follows (the classic continuation question in other years).
